intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 6 units · functions to interest

Grade 12 later does sequences, stats, coordinate geometry and matrices. This year is graphs of functions, plus similar triangles and money maths. Every worked box: *Given → formula → algebra → check forbidden values*.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.intro:
Exponential: f(x)=a^x, a>0, a≠1. Always positive. a>1 grows; 0<a<1 decays. y-intercept 1.

Log is the inverse: y=logₐx means a^y=x. Domain x>0. logₐ1=0, logₐa=1.

cards.title: Exponential Functions
body: An **exponential function** is f(x) = bˣ with base b > 0, b ≠ 1. The variable is in the exponent. Example: f(x) = 2ˣ gives 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8 for x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3.

**Graph facts:** domain all real numbers; range y > 0; y-intercept (0, 1); the x-axis (y = 0) is a horizontal asymptote. b > 1 → growth (increasing); 0 < b < 1 → decay (decreasing). y = (½)ˣ is the reflection of y = 2ˣ in the y-axis.
**Laws of exponents:** aᵐ·aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1; a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ; a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(aᵐ).

**Solving exponential equations — same base method:** write both sides as powers of the same base and equate the exponents. Example: 32^(x+1) = 128 → 2^(5x+5) = 2⁷ → 5x + 5 = 7 → x = 2/5. If the bases cannot be matched, take logs of both sides: 3ˣ = 20 → x = log 20 / log 3 ≈ 2.73.
Logarithm laws used with exponentials: log(MN) = log M + log N; log(M/N) = log M − log N; log(Mᵏ) = k log M.

cards.title: Change of base
body: logₐb = log b / log a (any legal base). On a calculator use ln or log₁₀ on both.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1: Express both sides with a base of 2**
$$32 = 2^5 \implies 32^{x+1} = (2^5)^{x+1} = 2^{5x + 5}$$
$$128 = 2^7$$

**Step 2: Equate the exponents**
Since the bases match, we can set the exponents equal:
$$5x + 5 = 7$$

**Step 3: Solve the linear equation**
$$5x = 2 \implies x = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$

**Step 4: Verify the solution**
$$32^{0.4 + 1} = 32^{1.4} = (2^5)^{1.4} = 2^7 = 128$$. The solution is valid.
**Result:** **$$x = 2/5$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the exact numerical value of the expression: $$\log_2\left(4 \times \sqrt[5]{4}\right) - \log_2\left(8^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Simplify the first logarithmic term**
$$\text{Term 1} = \log_2\left(4 \times \sqrt[5]{4}\right)$$
$$4 \times \sqrt[5]{4} = 2^2 \times (2^2)^{1/5} = 2^2 \times 2^{2/5} = 2^{2 + \frac{2}{5}} = 2^{12/5}$$
$$\log_2\left(2^{12/5}\right) = \frac{12}{5}$$

**Step 2: Simplify the second logarithmic term**
$$\text{Term 2} = \log_2\left(8^{1/3}\right)$$
$$8^{1/3} = (2^3)^{1/3} = 2^1 = 2$$
$$\log_2(2) = 1$$

**Step 3: Subtract the terms**
$$\text{Value} = \frac{12}{5} - 1 = \frac{12 - 5}{5} = \frac{7}{5}$$
**Result:** **$$7/5$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1: Express all terms with a base of 3**
$$(3^2)^3 = 3^{2 \times 3} = 3^6$$
$$9^2 = (3^2)^2 = 3^4$$
$$3^3 = 3^3$$

**Step 2: Apply laws of exponents**
$$\text{Expression} = 3^6 \times 3^4 \div 3^3$$
$$\text{Expression} = 3^{6 + 4 - 3} = 3^7$$

**Step 3: State final result**
The simplified expression is $$3^7$$.
**Result:** **$$3^7$$**.

cards.title: 4.2 The logarithmic function
body: **Definition:** for b > 0, b ≠ 1 and x > 0, $$\log_b x = y \iff b^y = x$$. A logarithm is an **exponent**: log₂ 8 = 3 because 2³ = 8. log₁₀ x is written log x (common log); logₑ x is written ln x (natural log).

The logarithmic function f(x) = log_b x is the **inverse** of the exponential function g(x) = bˣ. So its graph is the reflection of y = bˣ in the line y = x: **domain x > 0, range all real numbers**, x-intercept (1, 0), and the y-axis is a vertical asymptote. For b > 1 it increases; for 0 < b < 1 it decreases.
**Converting forms (step by step):** log₃ 81 = 4 ⇔ 3⁴ = 81; 5² = 25 ⇔ log₅ 25 = 2. To evaluate log₃ 9, ask "3 to what power gives 9?" → 2.
**Laws of logarithms** (M, N > 0): log_b(MN) = log_b M + log_b N; log_b(M/N) = log_b M − log_b N; log_b(Mᵏ) = k log_b M; log_b b = 1; log_b 1 = 0; change of base: log_b M = log M / log b.
**Domain of a transformed log:** the expression inside must be positive. f(x) = log₃(x − 4) needs x − 4 > 0, so the domain is x > 4 and the vertical asymptote is x = 4.
**Solving log equations:** write in exponential form, then check that the answer keeps every log argument positive. Example: log₂(x − 1) = 3 → x − 1 = 2³ = 8 → x = 9 (check: log₂ 8 = 3 ✔).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the domain of the logarithmic function $$f(x) = \log_3(x - 4)$$?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Set up the domain inequality**
The argument of a logarithmic function must be strictly positive:
$$x - 4 > 0$$

**Step 2: Solve the inequality**
Add $$4$$ to both sides:
$$x > 4$$

**Step 3: State in interval notation**
This corresponds to the open interval $$(4, \infty)$$.
**Result:** **$$(4, \infty)$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write in exponential form**
Let $$y = \log_3 9$$. This is equivalent to:
$$3^y = 9$$

**Step 2: Solve for $$y$$**
Since $$9 = 3^2$$:
$$3^y = 3^2 \implies y = 2$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
$$\log_3 9 = 2$$
**Result:** **$$2$$**.

cards.title: Logarithms
body: log_b x = y means b^y = x. The log is the inverse of the exponential. Domain x>0.

cards.title: Practice
cards.why:
**Exponential form:** 2x + 1 = 3² = 9, so 2x = 8 and x = 4.
**Check:** the argument 2(4) + 1 = 9 > 0 and log₃ 9 = 2 ✔.

cards.title: Log = exponent: "the base goes to the other side"
body: log_b x = y ⇔ b^y = x. Read it as a loop: **base b, raised to the answer y, gives x.**
Logs of products **add**, quotients **subtract**, powers come **down in front**.

lessons.title: Applications of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions

cards.title: 4.3 Applications of exponential and logarithmic functions
body: **Growth and decay model:** A = A₀(1 + r)ᵗ for growth at rate r per period, and A = A₀(1 − r)ᵗ for decay. A₀ is the starting amount and t the number of periods.
**Compound interest:** A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿᵗ where n is the number of compounding periods per year. Example: 1000 Nakfa at 10% per year compounded yearly for 2 years: A = 1000 × 1.1² = 1210 Nakfa.
**Population growth:** a town of 20 000 grows by 3% a year. After 5 years: 20 000 × 1.03⁵ ≈ 23 185 people.
**Half-life (radioactive decay):** the amount halves every half-life T: A = A₀(½)^(t/T). Example: 80 g with half-life 5 years, after 15 years: 80 × (½)³ = 10 g.
**Using logs to find the time:** when is 1000 Nakfa at 10% doubled? 1000 × 1.1ᵗ = 2000 → 1.1ᵗ = 2 → t = log 2 / log 1.1 ≈ 0.301/0.0414 ≈ 7.3 years.

**Logarithmic scales:** pH = −log[H⁺] (a solution with [H⁺] = 10⁻³ has pH 3); the Richter scale for earthquakes and the decibel scale for sound are also logarithmic — an increase of 1 on the Richter scale means 10 times the amplitude.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1: Express both sides with a base of 2**
$$4^{-3} = (2^2)^{-3} = 2^{-6}$$
So, the equation becomes:
$$2^{x^2 + 5x} = 2^{-6}$$

**Step 2: Equate the exponents**
$$x^2 + 5x = -6$$

**Step 3: Solve the quadratic equation**
$$x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0$$
$$(x + 2)(x + 3) = 0 \implies x = -2 \text{ or } x = -3$$
Both are valid real numbers.
**Result:** **$$x = -2$$ or $$x = -3$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Convert the logarithmic equation to its equivalent exponential form: $$\log_2 16 = 4$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Apply the logarithmic definition**
The relationship is defined by $$\log_a(x) = y \iff a^y = x$$.
Here, $$a = 2$$, $$x = 16$$, and $$y = 4$$.

**Step 2: Rewrite in exponential form**
$$2^4 = 16$$
**Result:** **$$2^4 = 16$$**.
